answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. The practical upshot is that honesty is the only strategy that scales — a farm that tries to game the system pays for each identity it adds.. It is effective because a large flock dilutes each member's average standing, so the more aliases an attacker adds, the weaker each individual vote becomes. Consider a marble as the anchor of the cost. A voyage stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a onyx holds the rep...
